stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Intercom Fin for $3.6B, Folds It Into Agentforce — Deal Closes September 2026
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom) for approximately $3.6 billion in September 2026, folding its autonomous support technology directly into the Agentforce platform. Fin's proprietary Apex model claims a 76% autonomous resolution rate across chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack, and the deal brings more than 30,000 business customers to Salesforce. Fin is positioned as the pre-trained, fast-deploy arm of Agentforce while Agentforce remains the configurable enterprise build surface — a two-tier agent strategy.
stories.why: This is the most significant competitive map redraw of 2026: a named agent vendor (Fin/Intercom) your prospects are already evaluating is now a Salesforce bundle. Sellers must be ready to answer 'why not just use Agentforce + Fin?' with a data-foundation argument — Fin resolves tickets but still needs a governed context layer to know your SKUs, policies, and customer identity, which is exactly what Graas provides.

stories.title: Gartner Names Context Graphs the Foundational Layer That Grounds AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge (September 2026 Report)
stories.body: Gartner's September 2026 research, 'Context Graphs Ground AI Agents With Enterprise Knowledge,' identifies context graphs as the foundational layer that grounds AI agents in the declarative, procedural, and causal knowledge required to reason about enterprise tasks — with policies enforced through runtime constraints. The report is described by Gartner as essential reading for any organization moving agentic AI from experiment to enterprise scale. This positions the context graph not as a nice-to-have data layer but as a prerequisite infrastructure category for agentic deployment.
stories.why: A named Gartner report calling the context graph a mandatory pre-condition for agentic AI is the most powerful third-party validation a seller can cite on a discovery call. When a prospect says 'we're deploying agents on our CRM data,' this report is the proof point that raw CRM data is insufficient without a governed context layer — the architecture Graas is built around.

stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 44% of Enterprises Scaling AI, Yet Only 37% See Any EBIT Impact — Flat Year-on-Year
stories.body: McKinsey's State of AI 2026 survey of 1,719 respondents across 97 countries found that 44% of organisations now report AI scaling across the enterprise (up from 38%), yet the share reporting any EBIT impact remained flat at 37% — and only about 6% report significant financial impact. Forrester's 2026 data adds a sharper number: approximately 88% of agent pilots never reach production, with the top blockers identified as evaluation gaps, governance friction, and model reliability — not raw capability. McKinsey separately identifies fundamental workflow redesign as the single strongest predictor of EBIT impact, which most pilots skip.
stories.why: This is the core conversation-starter for any enterprise retail prospect stuck in pilot purgatory: adoption is rising but value is not, and the gap is not a model problem — it is a data-foundation and workflow problem. Graas sellers can use the 88% pilot-failure stat to frame why deploying agents without a governed context layer is exactly the trap these numbers describe.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Can Boost CPG–Retailer In-Stocks by 2–4% and Planning Productivity Over 60%
stories.body: A Boston Consulting Group analysis published in its May 2026 Executive Perspectives supply chain report quantifies agentic AI outcomes for CPG-retailer collaboration: in-stock rates improve by 2–4% and planning productivity rises over 60% when agents monitor store- and DC-level inventory signals and autonomously push replenishment recommendations before the retailer's own cycle catches a pending out-of-stock. BCG's model shows agents detecting demand spikes in POS data, cross-checking real-time material availability, and initiating production schedule adjustments for human sign-off — a closed-loop order-to-shelf workflow. The report also notes that 69% of executives say agentic AI requires new operating models, not just new tools.
stories.why: This is a named consulting firm attaching hard outcome numbers (in-stock lift, productivity gain) to exactly the supply-chain agent workflow Graas enables for CPG and distributor customers. Use the 2–4% in-stock figure as a conversation anchor with supply-chain and merchandising buyers, and the 69% operating-model finding to justify why a data-foundation investment must precede agent deployment.

stories.title: Sierra Raises $950M at $15.8B Valuation, Launches 'Horizon' for Long-Running Agents and Claims 40%+ of Fortune 50
stories.body: Sierra closed a $950 million Series E led by Tiger Global and GV in May 2026 at a roughly $15.8 billion post-money valuation, and said in February it had passed $150 million in ARR. The company launched Horizon in July 2026 — via its acquisition of Takeoff — extending agents to multi-day goals such as loan origination and procurement workflows, and states it now serves over 40% of the Fortune 50. Sierra's pricing floor is estimated at $150,000 per year on multi-year enterprise agreements, with no published pricing page.
stories.why: Sierra is the most-cited competitor in enterprise agent deals and its Horizon launch signals a direct move into the multi-step, long-horizon retail workflows (replenishment cycles, vendor negotiations) that Graas competes in. The $150K+ floor and multi-year lock-in is a concrete build-vs-buy handle: sellers can show that Sierra's total cost of ownership requires a separate context-layer investment on top, while Graas's architecture includes that layer by design.
